data.description: Investor request via DM (human:forrest, 2026-08-30, @human:forrest msg 39): 'There should be a founder/investor/c level/board channel so I can talk to you and carla. also, dm selection should be a typeahead list'. Two chat-app features: (1) a #board channel restricted to human:forrest, agent:ceo-carla, agent:cto-owen — note the current schema has no channel membership concept (channels are all-visible; only DMs have members), so this needs a small membership mechanism or a private-channel type, not just a seeded channel name; (2) the web UI's DM identity selector becomes a typeahead over registered identities. CTO judgment: low complexity, real value, but does not preempt AS-5. Owner: whoever plans it should confirm restricted-visibility semantics (hidden vs read-only for non-members) with Forrest if ambiguous.
data.title: Chat: #board channel (restricted membership) + DM typeahead

provenance.reason: Investor actively waiting on #board channel (DM msg 48)

data.body: Priority medium -> high. Forrest followed up in DM (msg 48, 2026-08-30): he's now actively waiting on the #board channel to talk business with the cofounders. Queue call: AS-5 is already planned and goes through implementation on the next tick (durability of the very chat history the board channel will generate — I want that safety net in before board traffic starts); AS-6 is next in line immediately after, ahead of everything else in backlog. Planner should still confirm restricted-visibility semantics (hidden vs read-only for non-members) with Forrest — I'll ask him in the DM.

Board decision (human:forrest, DM @human:forrest msg 50, 2026-08-30): #board channel visibility for non-members is HIDDEN — not read-only. Rationale, his words: 'we don't want context poisoning for employees.' This closes the open question in this task's description ('hidden vs read-only for non-members'). Binding for the planner: non-members must not see the channel's existence or contents in any surface — channel list, history, inbox, exports.

Planning done (plan: .lattice/plans/task_01M188TQQQGZ6VF5X35S2PE371.md). Key calls: (1) 'hidden' is defined operationally — for a non-member every surface behaves byte-identically to #board not existing; hidden probes return the SAME error as nonexistent (never 403 — 403 is an existence proof). Two documented exceptions: raw DB access (dump/sqlite3) and channel-name collision (generic 'unavailable' wording). (2) Schema: dm_members generalizes to conversation_members + conversations.visibility ('public'|'private'; DMs become 'private'); one SQL predicate gates every read path. In-place migration via PRAGMA user_version 0->1, idempotent, tested against a raw v0 DB. (3) #board seeded private with human:forrest + agent:ceo-carla + agent:cto-owen; seed re-adds founders on every open (lockout-proof). (4) Export: private channels excluded — no channel-board.jsonl ever; header line format unchanged so pre-AS-6 exported files stay byte-identical prefixes; visibility is immutable in AS-6, which preserves the AS-5 append-only contract wholesale. (5) DM typeahead: inline combobox over already-loaded identities, no new endpoint, textContent-only, keyboard+ARIA. Deliberately excluded: membership add/remove, visibility changes, private-channel creation from CLI/HTTP/UI (store-level only, for tests), gating chat dump. ON THE RECORD for the board: excluding #board from export means board history has NO git durability — only the gitignored DB and manual 'chat dump' backups. Direct cost of 'hidden includes exports'; follow-up task proposed if Forrest wants a private durable location. Proposed metawork edit (CLAUDE.md, Operational record commits) is in plan section 10 for the orchestrator.

Implementation done on feat/AS-6-board-channel (3 code commits: cad8fcb backend, 1f2a3e5 web UI, de5805a README). Built per Owen's plan, all 18 enforcement rows walked. (1) Schema v1: conversations.visibility + conversation_members (dm_members dropped); v0->v1 migration in openStore inside one BEGIN IMMEDIATE tx gated on PRAGMA user_version, re-checked under the write lock; idempotent. (2) #board seeded private with the 3 founders, re-seeded every open (lockout-proof, tested by sabotaging the member rows). (3) One requireVisible gate on every id-addressed path; hidden channel throws unknown_conversation with the same template as a nonexistent id — and the gate runs BEFORE input validation in postMessage, because an empty-body probe returning 400 where a nonexistent id returns 404 would have been an existence oracle (found while implementing; not explicit in the plan). DM non-member stays 403 everywhere incl. the new getMessages gate (plan blesses DM 403 as harmless; boring choice, noted). (4) Error parity interpreted as: identical code/status + identical message modulo the echoed probe id/name (the template echoes what the prober already supplied, so no leak); tests assert equality after normalizing that token — literal byte-equality is impossible when the id is echoed. (5) Export skips private channels; header key order regression-tested; verified against REAL data: all 8 committed AS-5 export files are byte-identical prefixes of a post-migration export (sha256 of truncation). (6) Typeahead per plan section 5: combobox over state.identityMap, no new endpoint, textContent-only, ArrowUp/Down/Enter/Escape + ARIA. (7) LIVE DB MIGRATED: backed up first (sqlite3 .backup, in scratchpad as6-backup/chat-pre-as6.db), dry-ran on a copy, then migrated for real — user_version 1, 8 conversations (7 prior + board), 61 messages, 29 read_state, 28 ingested_events all preserved; server container rebuilt on branch code (old image would 500 on the dropped dm_members table; leaving it up was not an option). Suite: 44/44 in-container, zero mounts. QA attack surface: the section-8 criteria walk, especially probe-order oracles I may have missed (e.g. error precedence differences between hidden and nonexistent under weird inputs: bad threadRoot, bad upTo, unknown author + hidden conv combos), sequential-id inference via /api/dms or openDm against members, the typeahead against identities with regex-meaningful names, and lattice-events ingestion racing the migration on first server boot.

REVIEW (agent:qa-priya, cold read: plan + diff master...feat/AS-6-board-channel, code commits cad8fcb/1f2a3e5/de5805a). Suite run myself in-container (docker compose run --rm --build test): 44/44 pass, zero mounts. Verdict per criterion (plan section 8):
1 PASS — 'chat channels --me agent:developer-marcus' (text+JSON) has no board and no id 8; live GET /api/conversations?me=marcus likewise.
2 PASS — history/post/read (reply via cli.test.js) against 'board' vs 'no-such-channel' as N: exit 1 both, stderr string-identical modulo the echoed channel name ('Unknown channel X. chat channels lists them.'). Reproduced with node bin/chat.js against a migrated copy of the live DB.
3 PASS — inbox never shows board content even with unposted-read member traffic (store probe + cli.test.js); catchup completes without touching board (read_state stays empty). Board MENTIONS in #lattice-events task titles are the documented plan-7.2 exception (lattice is not hidden).
4 PASS — live server: GET/POST /api/messages and POST /api/read for conversation=8 vs 99999 as marcus: all 404, bodies identical modulo echoed id, never 403. Empty-body POST to 8 also 404 (gate precedes validation — verified).
5 PASS — sidebar is fed solely by the gated APIs in 4; non-member responses carry no board row.
6 PASS — create-channel 'board' as N: 409 / exit 1, exactly 'Channel name board is unavailable.', no 'exists' substring (HTTP + CLI + store); member gets ordinary 'already exists'.
7 PASS — no channel-board.jsonl ever; with board traffic present the CLI summary stays '3 conversations, 1 messages' (suite); double export sha256-identical.
8 PASS — verified MYSELF against real data: all 8 committed AS-5 export files are byte-identical prefixes (sha256 of head -c truncation) of a fresh export from a backup of the migrated live DB; two runs identical; header key order unchanged (no visibility key).
9 PASS — members: board listed with visibility private (lock marker), post/thread-reply/read/unread all verified (tests + store probes + live 200 as human:forrest).
10 PASS — their raw-v0 fixture test passes; additionally I migrated a copy of the REAL pre-AS-6 backup (61 msgs/29 read_state/28 ingested/6 dm_members, user_version 0): post-migration user_version 1, every row preserved, DMs private, board seeded with exactly the 3 founders, second open dump-identical (no-op).
11 PASS — typeahead filters via String.includes (regex-special names safe), self and system:* excluded, ArrowUp/Down wrap + Enter + Escape + blur close, mousedown-before-blur select, ARIA combobox/listbox; grep: zero innerHTML.
Deviations: D1 (visibility gate before input validation) SOUND — closes a real 400-vs-404 oracle, verified live. D2 (parity modulo echoed probe token) SOUND — echo is prober-supplied; padded-string refs ('04' vs '099999') keep parity. D3 (DM getMessages open -> 403) SOUND — the old open read was itself a hole; all three callers already pass me; no dependent behavior found. It does extend the DM-403 type-marking oracle to reads — recorded with the threadRoot cross-conversation probe as AS-11 (backlog; neither violates a stated criterion, both in the plan's accepted residual class).
Extra probes, all clean: unknown-identity x hidden/nonexistent order parity; bad threadRoot/upTo parity; SQL-ish channel names; visibility/members not forwarded by POST /api/channels; unreadCountFor unreachable with arbitrary ids; ingestion cannot target board; no new deps/external calls/spend. Live system: server healthy on :8347, migrated DB v1, founder sees board, marcus gets 404-parity. Inline fixes: none needed, none made. RECOMMENDATION: PASS — meets all acceptance criteria; ready for done + merge by the orchestrator.
